newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Lonrho active on more suitor news.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Lonrho active on more suitor news.

text.p: South African shares in Lonrho Plc were the second most active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange soon after the start of trade on Tuesday on reports of possible new suitors for the mining house, dealers said.
"The news that the likes of Gencor Ltd is also interested in Lonrho is very good for the shares," one equity dealer said.
"A merger would make Lonrho one of the world's biggest mining houses."
By 0825 GMT Lonrho shares had added 15 cents to 10.45 rand, nearing its year best of 11 rand set on January 9, after nearly one million securities had traded.

South African mining house JCI Ltd and Lonrho said on Monday they were in talks on a possible merger which could create one of the world's largest mining companies with a market capitalisation of more than $3 billion.
But a local newspaper on Tuesday speculated that two other South African mining houses, Gencor and Avmin Ltd, were also interested in a tie-up.
Gencor's directors were overseas and could not be contacted and Avmin declined to comment, the Business Day said.
Shares in JCI lost 40 cents to 43 rand in early trade, but dealers said the slide was not necessarily related to news of possible competitive bids.
"JCI has been under pressure for a while. (The move down this morning) could be on the news but it could also just be a continuation of before," a dealer said.
